_metadata.bestAvailable: finalBestAvailable = the hint that would be served now (preference rule over playable hints) or the reviewer's best non-playable hint; reviewerBestAvailable = the original blind reviewer's pick; correctionBestAvailable = a correction review's pick over its subset. None of these drives assembly.

pairs.pairNote: Solid, easy pair; the phrase-join on the CHARM side is about as familiar as phrases get.

clues.wordAConnection: A bracelet is a classic accessory.
clues.wordBConnection: A charm bracelet carries little charms.
clues.revealExplanation: A charm bracelet is an accessory hung with little charms.

blindReview.reason: ACCESSORY via a bracelet being a textbook accessory; CHARM via the instantly familiar 'charm bracelet'; clean and fair, if not surprising.

pairs.pairNote: Natural scene clue; CAMERA side is softer than AFRICA but still immediate once you picture a safari jeep.

clues.revealExplanation: Africa is famous for safaris, where you bring a camera to spot wildlife.

blindReview.reason: AFRICA via the iconic African safari; CAMERA via the photo safari scene of tourists snapping wildlife; clicks naturally.

pairs.pairNote: Excellent double meaning; one of the best in the batch.

clues.revealExplanation: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz, and the band Toto sang the hit "Africa."

blindReview.reason: AFRICA via the band Toto's hugely familiar (and meme-revived) hit "Africa", DOG via Dorothy's dog Toto; two unrelated meanings of one name meeting is a genuine 'oh, nice' click.

clues.revealExplanation: Africa is famous for its safaris, and Safari is Apple's web browser.

override.reason: owner-selected pair, x02 brief 2026-10-19: Africa is famous for its safaris, and Safari is Apple's web browser.

pairs.pairNote: Best of the HYENA pairs: both sides are specific to hyenas rather than to any animal.

clues.wordBConnection: The hyena's call sounds like laughter.
clues.revealExplanation: Hyenas roam Africa with a cackle that sounds like laughing at a joke.

blindReview.reason: AFRICA via the hyena as a savanna animal (Lion King); JOKE via the famous 'laughing hyena' cackle; a pleasing pairing of two strong routes.

pairs.pairNote: Ideal pair for SAFARI; both sides are direct.

clues.wordAConnection: Africa is famous for its safaris.
clues.revealExplanation: Safari is a web browser, and Africa is famous for its wildlife safaris.

blindReview.reason: AFRICA via the classic wildlife safari, WEB via Apple's Safari browser; a clean double meaning that matches the owner-approved INTERNET + AFRICA example.

pairs.pairNote: Excellent pair; nothing to change.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: A clean pun on two very well-known references, both accurate.

clues.wordBConnection: Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz
clues.revealExplanation: Toto is both the band behind "Africa" and Dorothy's little dog in The Wizard of Oz.

blindReview.reason: AFRICA via Toto's hit song "Africa" and WIZARD via Dorothy's dog Toto in The Wizard of Oz; both facts are correct and the double reference is a real aha.

pairs.pairNote: The explanation could also say that 'mole' is spy slang for an undercover agent, but it is accurate and charming as written.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Works on both the spy sense and the burrowing-animal pun.

clues.wordBConnection: Moles live their lives under the cover of soil
clues.revealExplanation: A secret agent goes undercover; a mole lives under cover, literally underground.

blindReview.reason: Agent via a secret agent going undercover; mole via the playful 'under cover' underground pun, and the spy sense of mole backs it up.

pairs.pairNote: Kids' cartoon is widely known to younger adults and families; older players may need the explanation, hence moderate.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Exact character link, very satisfying for anyone who knows the show.

clues.revealExplanation: In Phineas and Ferb, Perry the Platypus is secretly Agent P.

blindReview.reason: Perry the Platypus (PLATYPUS) is secret Agent P (AGENT) in Phineas and Ferb.

clues.revealExplanation: A fart is a little puff of air and the oldest joke in the book.

override.reason: x04 owner supplement (2026-10-19), 002: A fart is a little puff of air and the oldest joke in the book.

pairs.pairNote: Strong pair.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Two everyday senses of one word, both instantly recognised.

clues.wordAConnection: Your bags come round on the baggage carousel
clues.wordBConnection: The carousel is a classic carnival ride
clues.revealExplanation: One carousel carries suitcases, the other carries painted horses.

blindReview.reason: AIRPORT via the baggage carousel and CARNIVAL via the merry-go-round carousel; a satisfying double meaning.

pairs.pairNote: Excellent pair.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Ideal double meaning with both sides immediate.

clues.wordAConnection: Planes take off from an airport runway
clues.revealExplanation: A runway launches planes at the airport and outfits at a fashion show.

blindReview.reason: AIRPORT runways for planes and fashion runways for MODELS; a clean, satisfying double meaning.

clues.revealExplanation: Stitch is the little blue alien in Lilo & Stitch, and a needle makes a stitch.

override.reason: x04 owner supplement (2026-10-19), 084: Stitch is the little blue alien in Lilo & Stitch, and a needle makes a stitch.

pairs.pairNote: The STITCHES side relies on Stitch the name matching the plural common noun, but that is the kind of pun the owner welcomes; the 2025 live-action remake keeps it current.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Players complete 'Lilo & Stitch' and the alien follows; fun once seen.

clues.wordAConnection: Lilo adopts Stitch, a blue alien (Experiment 626)
clues.revealExplanation: Lilo's best friend Stitch is a little blue alien.

blindReview.reason: ALIEN because Lilo's companion Stitch is a blue alien; STITCHES through the name Stitch in Lilo & Stitch, a name-to-word pun.

pairs.pairNote: Fine. 'Swiss cheese' is a U.S. name for Emmental-style cheese, which does come from Switzerland, so the explanation holds. Watch the board for WATCH, ARMY, KNIFE, BANK or CHOCOLATE.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Two common compounds that share one adjective.

clues.wordBConnection: Swiss cheese, the one with holes
clues.revealExplanation: Switzerland gave us both the Swiss Alps and Swiss cheese.

blindReview.reason: Alps via the Swiss Alps, cheese via Swiss cheese; both are familiar phrases.

pairs.pairNote: Strong.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: The brand twist on AMAZON (players may think of the rainforest first) makes a satisfying reveal.

clues.wordAConnection: The Amazon Echo is a smart speaker
clues.wordBConnection: Bats find their way using echoes (echolocation)
clues.revealExplanation: Amazon sells the Echo, and bats navigate by listening to echoes.

blindReview.reason: Amazon via its Echo smart speaker, bat via echolocation; both facts are correct.

pairs.pairNote: Strong; the hint does not contain WOMAN, it only completes the title.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Turns AMAZON away from the online store toward mythology, a satisfying pivot.

clues.wordAConnection: Wonder Woman is an Amazon princess
clues.revealExplanation: Wonder Woman, Princess Diana, was raised among the Amazons.

blindReview.reason: WOMAN completes Wonder Woman; AMAZON because Diana is an Amazon princess of Themyscira.

pairs.pairNote: The two hints are the same route; serve one. Explanation for BACKWARDS could say 'drivers ahead' to be exact, but it is not wrong.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: Reads naturally on both sides (mirrors reverse; ambulance lettering is reversed) and the explanation is precise.

clues.wordAConnection: The word on the hood is lettered in reverse
clues.wordBConnection: A mirror reverses what it shows
clues.revealExplanation: The reversed lettering on an ambulance only reads properly in a mirror.

blindReview.reason: AMBULANCE via the mirror-reversed lettering on its hood and MIRROR via mirrors reversing images; the explanation is accurate.

clues.wordAConnection: AMBULANCE is printed backwards on the front of the vehicle
clues.revealExplanation: AMBULANCE is printed backwards so drivers can read it the right way round in their mirror.

blindReview.reason: AMBULANCE via its backwards-printed name and MIRROR via backwards mirror writing; same idea as REVERSE, slightly less elegant because a mirror 'reverses' more naturally than it makes things 'backwards'.

clues.wordAConnection: An ambulance means someone needs help.
clues.wordBConnection: To pray is to wish hard for something.
clues.revealExplanation: When an ambulance races past, you might say a little prayer that everyone is okay.

override.reason: x04 owner supplement (2026-10-19), 052: When an ambulance races past, you might say a little prayer that everyone is okay.

clues.wordBConnection: The eagle is a big bird of prey.

pairs.pairNote: A classic two-senses pairing: heavenly wings vs. hot wings.

clues.wordBConnection: Buffalo wings are spicy chicken wings.
clues.revealExplanation: Angels are pictured with wings, and buffalo wings are spicy chicken wings.

blindReview.reason: ANGEL via the feathered wings angels are drawn with, BUFFALO via buffalo wings the bar food; two unrelated senses that click instantly.

pairs.pairNote: Two good options; SHOULDER is preferred under the fewer-phrase-joins guidance.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: A scene rather than a phrase-join, exactly the style the owner wants more of, and it lands both sides at once.

clues.revealExplanation: Angel food cake is light and fluffy, while devil's food cake is dark and rich.

blindReview.reason: ANGEL: angel food cake; DEVIL: devil's food cake; a phrase-join, but both are instantly familiar U.S. cakes and the light/dark opposites make it satisfying.

previous.wordAConnection: Angel food cake
previous.wordBConnection: Devil's food cake
previous.revealExplanation: One light and fluffy, one dark and chocolatey: both are cakes.

revision.reason: name angel food and devil's food cake

revisionReview.reason: ANGEL via angel food cake and DEVIL via devil's food cake; both are instantly familiar and the light/dark opposites make a genuinely satisfying pairing.

clues.wordAConnection: The cartoon angel sits on one shoulder
clues.wordBConnection: The cartoon devil sits on the other shoulder
clues.revealExplanation: That classic cartoon conscience: an angel on one shoulder, a devil on the other.

blindReview.reason: ANGEL and DEVIL: the iconic cartoon conscience scene with an angel on one shoulder and a devil on the other; one image covers both.

correctionBestAvailable.why: A rare phrase-join that is exceptional: both cakes are household names and the good/evil contrast is delightful.

pairs.pairNote: The Angel side reads as a title join, but the football side is a scene, so overall it is a two-Charlies double reference.

reviewerBestAvailable.why: The Charlie Brown football gag makes it a real 'oh, nice'.

clues.wordAConnection: Charlie's Angels is a crime-fighting trio.
clues.wordBConnection: Lucy always pulls the football away from Charlie Brown.
clues.revealExplanation: Charlie's Angels fight crime, and Lucy always yanks the football away from Charlie Brown.

blindReview.reason: ANGEL via Charlie's Angels and FOOTBALL via Lucy pulling the football away from Charlie Brown; two famous Charlies, and the Peanuts gag is a lovely reveal.

pairs.pairNote: Strong; same board-collision caveat as the other PICNIC pairs.

pairs.pairNote: Solid, slightly less vivid than basket/blanket because TABLE has many other homes.
